summary: A blog post by Anne Thynne, an aquarium and reef-keeping hobbyist, explaining how a backyard pond can be turned into an aquaponic system that grows vegetables alongside fish. It covers the basic principle of aquaponics, the nitrogen cycle, and claimed benefits including water savings, faster plant growth, year-round food, algae control, income potential and reduced pollution. The page is hosted on the FoodCycler site and ends with a note distinguishing the FoodCycler electric food waste recycler from composters.
one_line: Blog post by Anne Thynne on turning a backyard pond into an aquaponic system that grows fish and vegetables together.
key_facts: Anne Thynne introduces herself as not the famous marine biologist and says she has kept fish in aquariums since childhood.
Anne Thynne was introduced to aquascaping and reef keeping in 2007.
Aquaponics is described as a sustainable farming activity that grows fishes and plants together in one system.
In aquaponics, fish feces become fertilizer for plants, and plants keep the water clean for the fish.
The article says growing provisions on water was used as far back as the Aztec era, with peninsulas where they grew beans, corn and tomatoes.
The article gives Iraq as a modern example, where Arabs grow food on rafts.
The article claims plants in an aquaponic pond grow 3 times faster than in soil.
The nitrogen cycle is described as fish feces broken down by bacteria into ammonia, then nitrite, then the less toxic nitrate.
The article claims an aquaponic system saves almost 90% of the water used for growing plants compared to conventional gardening.
Water is lost from an aquaponic pond only through evaporation from warm weather or plant transpiration.
The article says aquatic plants and vegetable plants can absorb nitrate, which limits algae growth because algae require a high level of nitrate to bloom.
The article says aquaponic ponds allow food to be grown throughout the year, with temperature regulated by a greenhouse or other means.
The article says the fish in an aquaponic pond act as a natural pesticide by taking care of bugs that could harm plants.
The article says selling fish and vegetables from an aquaponic pond can provide income, and that setup requires low capital.
The note's terminology section states the FoodCycler is a countertop electric food waste recycler and is not a composter.
